name: Trinity
description:
You are given an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ elements $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$. You can perform the following operation any number (possibly $$$0$$$) of times: Choose two integers $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$, where $$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$, and assign $$$a_i := a_j$$$. Find the minimum number of operations required to make the array $$$a$$$ satisfy the condition: For every pairwise distinct triplet of indices $$$(x, y, z)$$$ ($$$1 \le x, y, z \le n$$$, $$$x 
e y$$$, $$$y 
e z$$$, $$$x 
e z$$$), there exists a non-degenerate triangle with side lengths $$$a_x$$$, $$$a_y$$$ and $$$a_z$$$, i.e. $$$a_x + a_y \gt a_z$$$, $$$a_y + a_z \gt a_x$$$ and $$$a_z + a_x \gt a_y$$$.
input_specification: Each test consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$3 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of elements in the array $$$a$$$. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the elements of the array $$$a$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum number of operations required.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2032C — Trinity [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
